n: Jeremiah begins honestly: “Lord, You are always right—but let me argue my case with You. Why do the wicked prosper? Why do traitors live at ease?” Faith can include hard questions asked respectfully.

f.w: Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?

n: You planted them and they took root and bear fruit. You are always on their lips but far from their hearts—religious talk without real devotion.

f.w: thou art near in their mouth, and far from their reins
reins

n: But You know me, Lord; You’ve tested my heart. Drag them off like sheep to slaughter and set them apart for judgment.

f.w: tried mine heart

n: How long will the land suffer drought because of the people’s wickedness? Animals and birds are dying, because the people say, “God won’t see what happens to us.”

f.w: He shall not see our last end
f.g: Possibly “He (Jeremiah) won’t live to see our end”—mocking the prophet.

n: God answers with a challenge rather than an explanation: if racing against men on foot has worn you out, how will you compete with horses? If you stumble in safe country, what will you do in the Jordan’s thick jungle? Harder trials are coming—God is training Jeremiah’s endurance.

f.w: how canst thou contend with horses?
the swelling of Jordan
f.g: The dense thickets along the Jordan River, where lions lurked.

n: Even your own brothers and family have betrayed you and are shouting against you. Don’t trust them, even when they speak kindly.

f.w: thy brethren, and the house of thy father

n: Now God expresses His own grief: I have abandoned My house, left My inheritance, and handed the love of My life to her enemies. God feels the pain of the judgment He must send.

f.w: the dearly beloved of my soul

n: My people have turned on Me like a lion roaring in the forest, so I have turned away from her.

f.w: therefore have I hated it
f.g: A Hebrew way of saying “I have rejected it” or “turned away from it.”

n: My inheritance is like a strangely colored bird attacked by other birds of prey. Call the wild animals to come and devour! Israel, once distinct, is now a target.

f.w: a speckled bird
f.g: A bird of unusual color, mobbed by others; or a hyena’s lair.

n: Many shepherds (foreign rulers) have ruined God’s vineyard, trampled His field, and turned His lovely land into a wasteland.

f.w: Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard

n: The desolate land mourns to God, because no one cares—no one takes it to heart.

f.w: no man layeth it to heart

n: Destroyers swarm over the bare hills; the Lord’s sword devours from one end of the land to the other. No one has peace.

f.w: no flesh shall have peace

n: They planted wheat but harvested thorns; they worked themselves sick for nothing. They will be ashamed of their meager crops because of God’s anger.

f.w: They have sown wheat, but shall reap thorns

n: God now speaks about Judah’s “evil neighbors”—nations that plundered Israel’s land. He will uproot them too, and uproot Judah from among them.

f.w: all mine evil neighbours
f.g: Neighboring nations such as Edom, Moab, Ammon, and the Philistines.

f.w: I will pluck them out

n: Then, surprisingly, God will have compassion on them as well and bring each nation back to its own land. His mercy extends beyond Israel.

f.w: I will return, and have compassion on them

n: If those nations will truly learn the ways of God’s people and swear “As the Lord lives,” as they once taught Israel to swear by Baal, they will be established among God’s people. Gentiles can be grafted in.

f.w: then shall they be built in the midst of my people

n: But any nation that won’t obey will be completely uprooted and destroyed.

f.w: I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation
